claims.text: Role in MS: spasticity: escalating doses of baclofen or tizanidine;
claims.quote: Spasticity is treated with escalating doses of baclofen or tizanidine.

claims.text: botulinum toxin injections if oral tx fails.
claims.quote: Injectable botulinum toxin in spastic muscles is used if oral therapies are ineffective

claims.text: Baclofen dose, spasticity (titration and max): Titrate: 5 mg t.i.d. 3 days, 10 mg t.i.d. 3 days, 15 mg t.i.d. 3 days, 20 mg t.i.d. 3 days.
claims.quote: 5 mg t.i.d. for 3 days 10 mg t.i.d. for 3 days 15 mg t.i.d. for 3 days 20 mg t.i.d. for 3 days

claims.text: Start low and ↑ gradually until optimum effect (usually 40 to 80 mg daily).
claims.quote: Start therapy at a low dosage and increase gradually until optimum effect is achieved (usually between 40 to 80 mg daily).

claims.text: Max total daily dose 80 mg (20 mg q.i.d.).
claims.quote: the total daily dose should not exceed a maximum of 80 mg daily (20 mg q.i.d.).

claims.text: Lowest dose compatible w optimal response recommended; slowly withdraw if no benefit after a reasonable trial.
claims.quote: The lowest dose compatible with an optimal response is recommended. If benefits are not evident after a reasonable trial period, patients should be slowly withdrawn from the drug

claims.text: Baclofen CI and key warnings: CI: hypersensitivity to baclofen.
claims.quote: Hypersensitivity to baclofen.

claims.text: Hallucinations and seizures have occurred on abrupt withdrawal — reduce dose slowly when discontinuing.
claims.quote: Hallucinations and seizures have occurred on abrupt withdrawal of baclofen. Therefore, except for serious adverse reactions, the dose should be reduced slowly when the drug is discontinued.

claims.text: Primarily excreted unchanged by kidneys — give w caution; may be necessary to reduce the dosage.
claims.quote: Because baclofen is primarily excreted unchanged through the kidneys, it should be given with caution, and it may be necessary to reduce the dosage.

claims.text: Neonatal withdrawal (↑ muscle tone, tremor, jitteriness, seizure) reported hours to days after delivery in neonates of mothers treated throughout pregnancy.
claims.quote: Withdrawal symptoms have been reported starting hours to days after delivery in neonates whose mothers were treated with oral baclofen throughout pregnancy. The symptoms of withdrawal in these infants have included increased muscle tone, tremor, jitteriness, and seizure.

claims.text: Baclofen precautions: Sedation possible — caution w driving/machinery; CNS effects may be additive to alcohol and other CNS depressants.
claims.quote: Because of the possibility of sedation, patients should be cautioned regarding the operation of automobiles or other dangerous machinery, and activities made hazardous by decreased alertness. Patients should also be cautioned that the central nervous system effects of baclofen may be additive to those of alcohol and other CNS depressants.

claims.text: Epilepsy: monitor clinical state and EEG at regular intervals (deterioration in seizure control/EEG reported occasionally).
claims.quote: In patients with epilepsy, the clinical state and electroencephalogram should be monitored at regular intervals, since deterioration in seizure control and EEG have been reported occasionally in patients taking baclofen.

claims.text: Baclofen overdose: OD signs: vomiting, muscular hypotonia, drowsiness, accommodation disorders, coma, respiratory depression, seizures.
claims.quote: Signs and Symptoms: Vomiting, muscular hypotonia, drowsiness, accommodation disorders, coma, respiratory depression, and seizures.

claims.text: OD tx: empty stomach (emesis then lavage) if alert; if obtunded secure airway w cuffed endotracheal tube b4 lavage (do not induce emesis); maintain respiratory exchange; do not use respiratory stimulants.
claims.quote: In the alert patient, empty the stomach promptly by induced emesis followed by lavage. In the obtunded patient, secure the airway with a cuffed endotracheal tube before beginning lavage (do not induce emesis). Maintain adequate respiratory exchange, do not use respiratory stimulants.

claims.text: Tizanidine (Zanaflex) dose, spasticity: Start 2 mg PO every 6 to 8 h as needed, max three doses in 24 h.
claims.quote: The recommended starting dose is 2 mg by mouth every 6 to 8 hours, as needed, to a maximum of three doses in 24 hours.

claims.text: ↑ by 2 mg to 4 mg per dose every 1 to 4 days; max total daily dose 36 mg.
claims.quote: Dosage can be gradually increased every 1 to 4 days by 2 mg to 4 mg at each dose based on clinical response and tolerability. The maximum total daily dosage is 36 mg.

claims.text: Renal impairment (CrCl <25 mL/min) or hepatic impairment: use lower individual doses during titration; ↑ individual doses rather than frequency.
claims.quote: Patients with renal impairment (creatinine clearance <25 mL/min) or hepatic impairment: use lower individual doses during titration. If higher doses are required, individual doses rather than dosing frequency should be increased.

claims.text: Monitor aminotransferase levels at baseline and 1 month after max dose is achieved.
claims.quote: Monitoring of aminotransferase levels is recommended at baseline and 1 month after maximum dose is achieved
claims.locator: 2.1 Recommended Evaluation and Testing Before and After Initiating Zanaflex

claims.text: Tizanidine (Zanaflex) CI: strong CYP1A2 inhibitors.
claims.quote: Zanaflex is contraindicated in patients taking strong CYP1A2 inhibitors

claims.text: CI: Hx of hypersensitivity to tizanidine or ingredients (anaphylaxis, angioedema).
claims.quote: with a history of hypersensitivity to tizanidine or the ingredients in Zanaflex. Symptoms have included anaphylaxis and angioedema

claims.text: Tizanidine (Zanaflex) key warnings: Hypotension risk minimized by dose titration; monitor for hypotension signs/symptoms prior to dosage increase.
claims.quote: The risk of hypotension may be minimized by dose titration; monitoring for signs and symptoms of hypotension prior to dosage increase may minimize the risks associated with hypotension.

claims.text: Monitor for hypotension w concurrent antihypertensive therapy.
claims.quote: Monitor for hypotension when Zanaflex is used in patients receiving concurrent antihypertensive therapy.

claims.text: May cause liver injury — monitor ALTs; discontinue if liver injury occurs.
claims.quote: Risk of liver injury: monitor ALTs; discontinue Zanaflex if liver injury occurs

claims.text: CNS depressant effects w alcohol and other CNS depressants (e.g., benzodiazepines, opioids, tricyclic antidepressants) may be additive.
claims.quote: The CNS depressant effects of Zanaflex with alcohol and other CNS depressants (e.g., benzodiazepines, opioids, tricyclic antidepressants) may be additive

claims.text: May cause hallucinations — consider discontinuing Zanaflex.
claims.quote: Consider discontinuing Zanaflex in patients who develop hallucinations.

claims.text: Withdrawal (rebound hypertension, tachycardia, hypertonia): decrease dose slowly, esp after high doses (20 to 28 mg daily) for long periods (9 weeks or more) or w narcotics.
claims.quote: To minimize the risk of these reactions, particularly in patients who have been receiving high doses of Zanaflex (20 to 28 mg daily) for long periods of time (9 weeks or more) or who may be on concomitant treatment with narcotics, the Zanaflex dosage should be decreased slowly

claims.text: Tizanidine (Zanaflex) interactions and overdose: Strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin) ↑ tizanidine exposure — significantly ↓ BP, ↑ drowsiness, ↑ psychomotor impairment.
claims.quote: Changes in pharmacokinetics of tizanidine when administered with a strong CYP1A2 inhibitor resulted in significantly decreased blood pressure, increased drowsiness, and increased psychomotor impairment

claims.text: OD: ↓ sensorium (lethargy, somnolence, confusion, coma), depressed cardiac function (most often bradycardia, hypotension), respiratory depression.
claims.quote: In the majority of cases, a decrease in sensorium was observed including lethargy, somnolence, confusion, and coma. Depressed cardiac function is also observed including most often bradycardia and hypotension. Respiratory depression is another common feature of tizanidine overdose.
